html:
Lusaka became the capital of Northern Rhodesia in 1935, replacing Livingstone, and grew from a small railway stop into the capital of independent Zambia.

The colonial government chose it for its central place on the railway line and its healthy plateau, and planned a garden city for officials, with African workers kept to compounds on the edges.

After independence it grew fast as people came from the countryside. Under Kenneth Kaunda it hosted the exiled leaders of liberation movements from Zimbabwe, Namibia, South Africa and Angola, including the headquarters of the ANC. It is the political and business centre of Zambia.
sum: Lusaka became the capital of Northern Rhodesia in 1935, replacing Livingstone, and grew from a small railway stop into the capital of independent Zambia.
